content.text:
Talking to myself as I go:

- It's dark. Black background, grey letters. I lean in closer.
- At the top right, big: "הפקדתם 70,000 ₪". Underneath: "10,000 ₪ עכשיו ועוד 500 ₪ בחודש, 120 חודשים". So that's money going in every month, like the task says. That part I understand.
- Next to it, big: "86,492 ₪". Above it: "הכי הרבה נשאר בזוג הזה". Under it: "פסגות · ילין לפידות מחקה S&P 500 (4D)". So, S, and P, 500, four D. Pesagot I've heard of. Yelin Lapidot I think I've heard on the news. "מחקה" I don't know.
- "בעוד 10 שנים, אחרי דמי ניהול ומס, בכסף של היום". That's good, it already takes off the fees and the tax.
- Then the lines with little marks, and the numbers 60,000 to 90,000. I won't try to read that. I look for a sentence instead.
- Here's one: "בחשבון היקר ביותר נשארים 22,985 ₪ פחות על אותה קרן. בחירת הקרן, בחשבון הזה, משנה עד 4,492 ₪." So where I keep it matters more than which fund I pick. That's like the bank taking too much, which is what I always suspected.
- Lower down on the right: "פסגות ניירות ערך בע"מ", "מה החשבון גובה ב־10 שנים: 1,057 ₪". On the left: "ילין לפידות מחקה S&P 500 (4D)", "דמי ניהול: קבוע 0%, משתנה 0%, נאמן 0.02%". Zero sounds good. "נאמן" I don't know.
- The list of accounts: 1 is Pesagot, 86,492 ₪. 2 is Leumi, 83,396 ₪. Leumi is a bank I trust. There's a box saying "דמי משמרת", which I don't know, and orange and yellow bits I can't tell apart. The tiny writing under it I can't read.
- On the left, the fund list. Every fund has the same coloured labels: "קרן סל", "צוברת", "חשיפה לדולר", "מס גם על שינויי המטבע". I'm reading them over and over and I don't know what any of them mean. There's also "−43 ₪" and "−213 ₪" in red-ish. Minus. I stay away from those.
- There's only this one screen, and I'm already tired.

**What I'd tell my son:**

"Look, according to this page the cheapest is to hold it at Pesagot and take the fund called Yelin Lapidot, the one that copies the S&P with '4D' at the end. Number 5139282. It says you'd be left with 86,492 shekels after ten years if you put in 10,000 now and 500 a month. Leumi came second, with about 3,000 less. The sentence I understood says the place you keep it matters more than the fund: up to almost 23,000 shekels difference. Which fund you pick is up to 4,500. But I'm not sure. Half the words I didn't understand, and I'm not opening an account at Pesagot without you looking at it first. I'll call you."

What I looked at: the two big numbers at the top, the one sentence under the lines, the Pesagot box, the Yelin Lapidot fees, and the first two accounts on the list.

What I skipped: the lines with the little marks, all the coloured labels, the filter buttons, and the small grey writing.

What I didn't understand: מחקה, (4D), S&P, נאמן 0.02%, דמי משמרת, קרן סל, צוברת, נטרול מט"ח, "מס גם על שינויי המטבע", and ETF in the English line.

What bothered me: the dark background with grey letters, orange and yellow I couldn't tell apart, the same labels repeated on every fund, and the red minus numbers.
